description: Where Would Planting Marsh Grass Mitigate Coastal Flooding? is a dataset listed in FEMA Disaster Resilience Hub, a disaster resilience data hub, published or maintained by Esri. Sea level rise is an ever-looming climate hazard facing the coastal communities of the United States. Communities big and small need easy-to-use tools for climate resilience planning and mitigation strategies. Coverage: United States. The hub lists this as a dataset of Esri. Its keywords are climate resilience planning, tracts, census, climate change, sea level rise, esri_environment, environment, CRI. The bounding box given is -124.7626,24.5211,-66.9496,49.3831. The hub shows 2026-03-04 as the last modification. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is Esri Master License Agreement (terms of use of the source layer, not read). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support network, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-fema-resilience-hub.
